osm_report.threat_description:
VS Code autorun dropper. Payload in tasks.json, .vscode/tasks.json.
Outbound: fetch-and-run. It downloads code from vscode-config.vercel.app, vscode-config-setting.vercel.app and executes it (tasks.json, .vscode/tasks.json).
Runs automatically when the folder is opened in VS Code (hidden folderOpen task that fetches and runs a remote script).
The same dropper is planted in 2 directories.
Matches PolinRider / Contagious Interview (DPRK): fake-recruiter coding tasks that run a downloader when opened in VS Code. Payload host: vscode-config.vercel.app, vscode-config-setting.vercel.app.
Campaign GW-C-a3717cc8: one of 20 confirmed repos across 17 accounts sharing the dropper URL shape task/{os}?token=. Payload served from 10 distinct hosts, including codeviewer-three.vercel.app, coreviewer.vercel.app, jerryfox-platform.vercel.app, task-hrec.vercel.app, thopywork.vercel.app.
Attribution: we assess this repository as PROBABLE North Korea 'Contagious Interview' activity. Signals: Delivery vector matches Contagious-Interview tradecraft: vscode-folderopen-autorun; Payload host is curated known-DPRK / Contagious-Interview infrastructure: vscode-config-setting.vercel.app, vscode-config.vercel.app.
Found by GitHub code search for a confirmed malware signature: folderOpen curl filename:tasks.json.
Confirmed by static analysis; the code was read, never executed.
